title: Receivables: fields read from each document and client file
description: receivables does not write documents; it reads the workspace's documents/<client>/*.json, merged over profiles/me.json and clients/<client>.json like the invoice CLI. Only the fields below are read and type-checked. Other fields belong to invoice-generator (see its --schema), so unknown fields are allowed here instead of rejected.

docType.description: invoice, debit_note and export_invoice add to what the client owes; receipt and credit_note reduce it; proforma and quotation are ignored

invNo.description: Document number; receipts and notes point to it with refInvoice

date.description: Document date, YYYY-MM-DD; documents dated after --as-of are left out

due.description: a date as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty (then the invoice date counts as the due date)

items.description: Line items; amount = qty × rate, as on the PDF

taxMode.description: GST mode; GST is added to the total and left out of the TDS base

refInvoice.description: Receipts and credit/debit notes: the invoice number they settle or adjust

tds.description: Receipts: income tax the client deducted at source from this payment, in rupees. The invoice counts as settled by amount received + tds

tdsSection.description: Rule id from rules/tds-sections.json the client deducts under; set it on the client file or on a receipt to check the TDS rate

currency.description: a 3-letter currency code like USD; default INR

exchangeRate.description: Rupees per unit of currency; converts foreign balances to rupees and INR receipts to the invoice currency

toName.description: Client name, used in the report and reminders
